PUMP (2007) by DAVID ADEY. David Adey transforms an ordinary football into a strange kinetic sculpture. Its surface is densely covered with drywall screws, while a hidden respirator repeatedly inflates and deflates the ball, producing a slow, mechanical rhythm. The Kinetic Grand Championship—often called the "Triathlon of the Art World"—is a legendary, 3-day, 50-mile race where human-powered, all-terrain art sculptures traverse land, sand dunes, mud, and water.  The event takes place annually over Memorial Day Weekend, officially kicking off at noon on the Arcata Plaza. Race Schedule & RouteDay 1 (Saturday):  Begins at 9:00 a.m. with art displays and judging on the Arcata Plaza. At exactly 12:00 noon, the race officially begins. Racers navigate the Arcata Bottoms and the grueling Manila dunes before crossing the Samoa Bridges into Eureka, ending at Halvorsen  Park.Day 2 (Sunday): Competitors tackle the water segment on the Humboldt Bay near the Eureka waterfront. Racers then tackle steep land inclines like Hookton Hill before heading to a private racer campout. Day 3 (Monday): Starts near Crab Park, sending racers over land to cross the Eel River, followed by a final stretch into Victorian Ferndale, where they cross the Main Street finish line. Let me know in the comments if you’re in the race, watching the races and which vehicle is your favorite. #kineticgrandchampionship #arcata #california #humboldtcounty #memorialdayweekend
